reason: The Agent contract, the live registry, the factory seat and the agent event vocabulary are kept as Go package internal/agent; the AsyncLocalStorage initiator becomes a serialisable reference carried in context.Context.

The one shipped driver is kept as component agent.driver: one goroutine per agent runs the turn and step state machine, the durable inbox, creation, resume and teardown, with a turn budget and a bounded final flush added.

The default model stays a small component with live config; it is one global service read with the agent scope key, a preset registers its own default as a scoped registration, and saving goes through config.Service.Apply of the boot area, whose result is returned.

The package is a deprecated selector between native schemas and the run_code form. The owner decision removes the run_code form, so one tool form remains and the executor is chosen by composition; nothing is left to select.
The deprecated Config type of the presentation selector has no Go counterpart because the selector component is not built.
The deprecated runtime schema of the presentation selector has no Go counterpart because the selector component is not built.
The deprecated selector module is not carried into Go; presets compose the executor directly, which is what the deprecation notice asks upstream users to do.
The deprecated apply function that mounts one of two executors has no Go counterpart because the selector component is not built.

The deprecated agent/request waterfall is not built. Model and effort use Model().Select, output cap and sampling use the controls in ModelSelection, model-switch detection uses PreStepRequest.Previous, and observers use step/start and the Start frame.
The default is no longer one per process: the driver finds the default-model service through the agent's scope, so a preset composition can mount its own instance.
Saving no longer depends on an optional editor: Save writes to the loader's one writable layer, which every profile has, and a failed write is returned as an error instead of being a silent no-op.

The batch contract lets a tool classify a call as parallel with read or write resource keys, and the scheduler treats a key conflict as a barrier, so safety that depends on a sibling call no longer forces exclusive. The executor is area A03's; the spec says to reopen this row if A03 keeps a unary classifier.

Teardown flushes the session within a bound before the write lease is released, and the driver component injects the store so the tree keeps it alive until the driver's cleanup returns; a flush failure is returned with the last durable seq.

A closed step with an unanswered call cannot be written: the missing results and step/end are one atomic batch on the step's single close path. No older inconsistent logs exist because the Go store reads no upstream session.

Every configured agent has a required start field (fresh, resume-or-create or resume) with no default, so a new session at every start is a written choice and resume-or-create derives a stable id from the label.
A configured agent may name a preset, which gives it its own persona, prompt sections and tool set through the same scoped composition a programmatic creator uses.
The driver has a built-in budget: steps per turn (default 500), attempts per step (default 8) and an optional time limit; a step limit ends the turn between steps with reason budget.
There is no PTC runtime for a preset to wait for: the owner decision replaces the guest runtime with an external command line, so the pending-selection state cannot occur.

Identity is a serialisable agent reference (session id plus incarnation) that each boundary carries and resolves on arrival; a child process gets it through the call token, so crossing a boundary has one stated mechanism.

The context carries a reference and not the live object; Registry.Resolve fails for a disposed or replaced agent, and the context itself is cancelled when the agent leaves, so stale identity cannot be used as a live agent.
WaitIdle and Dispose called from inside that agent's own Created dispatch return an error at once, so the documented deadlock becomes an immediate, testable failure.
Cancel takes a required inbox choice (Keep or Discard) and a scope (Turn or Step); a step-scope cancel closes the step with paired results and lets the turn continue when steering is pending.

The driver never merges messages, and the design requires a message source with a kind and a list of producers, so a producer that merges contributions names all of them. The message type is area A04's and is listed as a dependency.
Kept as the notify event driver.StartFailed with the label, session id and error, so a consumer that buffers work for a configured identity can reject it instead of waiting.
Kept as the notify event agent.StreamFrame: Start, Chunk with a dense index and exactly one End sent after the durable record is committed; frames stay live-only.
Kept as the ordered event agent.Created: listeners run one at a time, the first error fails creation and rolls it back, and no turn starts before the dispatch has settled.
Kept as the notify event agent.Disposed, sent at teardown step T7 after the final flush and after the registry entry is removed, and only when Created had begun.
Kept as the notify event agent.Failed, which reports a step or turn failure also when it has no position in the log, for example a failed append.
Kept as the notify event agent.InboxClaimed, one per message, sent after the claim splice is committed in the turn-opening batch.
Kept as the notify event agent.InboxDiscarded, which now also carries the cancel cause recorded on the discard splice.
Kept as the notify event agent.InboxInserted with the message and the seq of its splice, queued under the inbox mutex and delivered outside it.
Kept as the around event agent.PreStep with a request type and the closed decisions Enter and Reject; Reject now carries a reason that is logged on turn/end.
Upstream marks the waterfall deprecated and forbids new listeners. It is the one place a request could differ from the log, so it is not built; each of its four uses has a named replacement.
Kept as the around event agent.AttemptFailed with the closed decisions GiveUp and Retry; the driver, not the listener, waits the back-off and caps attempts per step.
Kept as the notify event agent.StatusChanged with the two values idle and running; a separate lifecycle state says whether the agent accepts input.

Kept as the around event agent.TurnStopping behind a merging helper, with the closed decisions AllowStop and KeepOpen; a listener can only keep the turn open, so listener order cannot change the outcome.

The event is emitted inside upstream's browser application when its gateway connects. The Go UI has no client runtime; a reconnecting tab resumes the event stream by sequence number or receives a reset from the host.
A cordis internal event used to see a fiber's config candidate. The Go port offers the owned OnConfig hook for the same purpose; it is not an agent event.

A cordis internal hook that sees every dispatch. Its one upstream user vetoes an event by throwing from an observer; in Go an event that may be vetoed has a closed decision type, so the hook is not provided.
A cordis internal event that upstream components use to learn that a fiber is leaving. In Go each fiber has a cancellation context, and the remaining uses get an owned subscription.
A cordis internal event about service availability. The Go port already has the subscription and gives it a form owned by the subscribing fiber.

A cordis internal event about fiber state changes. The Go port already has the subscription and gives it an owned form; the agent registry's own use disappears because the initiator is a context value.
A loader event that tells a component one of its live config fields changed. In Go a component accepts an in-place update through its update hook.
The event is emitted and consumed inside upstream's browser application when the user changes language. The Go host renders HTML in the chosen language, so there is no client event.
The event is emitted by upstream's client UI renderer when a slot registration changes and has no consumer. The Go UI composes templates on the host and has no client slot registry.
The event is emitted and consumed inside upstream's browser application when the theme changes. In the Go UI the theme is a host preference applied when the page is rendered.
Replaced by the Go struct defaultmodel.Config with provider and model required and reasoningEffort optional, all live fields.

Replaced by the Go struct driver.Config: maxParallelToolCalls moves to the tools component as maxParallel (live, default 10) so that the cap has one owner, agents[] gains a required start mode and an optional preset, and the budget and flush bounds are added.
The schema has one field that selects between native schemas and the run_code form. With one tool form left there is nothing to configure, so no Go struct exists.
Replaced by service key defaultmodel.Key with Current (by scope key), Register (a scoped default) and Save; Save calls config.Service.Apply of the boot area and returns its result.
The Go driver exposes no service of its own: it fills the registry's factory seat and reads its limits from its component config, so consumers cannot depend on the driver.
Replaced by service key agent.Agents and the Registry interface (Create, Resume, Get, Resolve, List, SetFactory), with the owner passed explicitly.

The service hosts a DevTools debugging target and a cordis tree query interface for the experimental inspector. The target is not built in Go; tree queries are the loader's lookup interface and process inspection uses the Go profiler endpoints.
Kept: admission is one logged batch after the model call is bound, the request is built from the log alone, and no hook can change a request between admission and dispatch.
summary: Anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log and the objects it references.

reason: Go has no AsyncLocalStorage. The initiating agent is a reference value in context.Context, which needs no drain bookkeeping at teardown; explicit identity stays authoritative at every boundary.
summary: The agent that started an operation is carried implicitly through asynchronous calls with AsyncLocalStorage.

reason: Kept: Inject is the only way to add context, it logs a splice and opens no turn, and a turn means one run of the model loop.
summary: inject() is the only way to add supplementary model-facing input, and a turn means exactly one execution of the model loop.

reason: Kept: a send only queues and returns a receipt that proves admission; a result exists only for a caller that owns the interval from receipt to idle, which the SDK and command-line areas define.
summary: Sending a follow-up only enqueues the message; no single message owns the activity that follows.

reason: Kept: a cancelled stream commits the delivered text and reasoning as an interrupted assistant message, leaves tool calls out, and records an attempt when nothing was delivered.
summary: When a model stream is cancelled, the text the user already saw is committed as an assistant message marked interrupted.

reason: Kept: setup receives the scope and the agent as separate parameters, events carry their agent, and a scope context has no reverse accessor for its agent.
summary: Agent identity is passed explicitly wherever it is needed; a context owns registrations and cleanup only.

reason: Kept: Created is an ordered, awaited dispatch whose failure fails creation. One change: waiting for the agent or disposing it from inside its own creation returns an error instead of deadlocking.
summary: Agent creation runs its initialization listeners one at a time and waits for each; a failure fails creation.

reason: Kept in the driver's admission step: at a series start the prompt node is rewritten only when its effective text must move, which preserves the provider's cached prefix.
summary: At the start of a new request series the first system message is rewritten only when the effective prompt text must move.

reason: Kept: opt-in per call, fail to exclusive, bounded pool, results committed in model order. Extended with optional read and write resource keys, which the note's tagged mode was kept to allow.
summary: Sibling tool calls may run in parallel when each tool's classifier says so; anything else is exclusive.

reason: Kept in the driver's admission step: on a route that declares the capability a changed prompt is appended in history; the capability is read from the bound call, which area A04 supplies.
summary: For a model route that declares the capability, a changed system prompt is appended later in the history instead of rewriting message 0.

reason: Kept: an agent's id is its session's id. The Go reference adds an incarnation number so a replaced agent with the same id cannot be mistaken for the old one.
summary: A live agent and its session share one identifier.

reason: Kept: a turn claims at most one queued prompt in the same batch as turn/start, and the next turn opens only after the previous turn's flush has settled.
summary: Each send creates its own queue item and, if it runs, its own turn; two sends are never silently combined.

reason: The rule of one invocation form per agent holds trivially: the owner decision removes the run_code form, so native schemas are the only form and the mode setting disappears. The first verdict of ported predates that decision.
summary: Each agent offers its tools in exactly one form: native function schemas or a single run_code tool.

reason: Adopted for this area: no test sleeps (virtual time), a replay helper runs after every driver test, and the inbox and driver tests run under the race detector with repetition.
summary: Proposal: tests wait for events instead of sleeping, every loop test's log is replayed, and a stress job repeats the loop tests.

title: A contract package, a live registry and one replaceable driver
A turn and a step each have one close path, and admission is one batch
The inbox is a logged queue; a send returns a receipt; one follow-up is at most one turn
Three interception points with closed decisions; the request hook is removed
Cancellation carries a typed cause, an explicit inbox choice and a scope
One teardown order, shared by both owners
A built-in turn budget, finite by default
Shutdown flushes the final events within a bound, and reports when it cannot
Identity is an explicit, serialisable reference; the initiator is a context value
Model selection is logged, captured once per step, and falls back to a scoped default
No presentation selector; one tool form; a batch contract with resource keys
A configured agent states how it starts and which preset it uses
Units assigned here by default belong to the framework and the browser
Any component can find, address and own agents through one contract
Input can be sent at any time, is durable at once, and runs at most once
Every turn and step is bracketed, bounded and closed on every path
Extensions can steer a turn through three typed points and observe the rest
A turn or a single step can be stopped, and the log says why
Agents are created, resumed and torn down as one transaction, and shutdown keeps the last events
Each step uses one logged model selection
A fresh agent has a default model, and saving a new default survives a restart
An operator declares standing agents in configuration and chooses how each starts
A step's tools are fixed once, and its calls run in a bounded, ordered batch
Registry create, get, list, id collision, and dispose only through the handle
Initiator in context; Resolve refuses a disposed or replaced incarnation
Agent events reach only that agent's scope and global listeners
Concurrent sends and cancel: splice order equals receipt order, fold equals state, a message id seen anywhere in history is refused with the first receipt, no race
Two follow-ups give two turns; the second opens after the first turn's flush
An injection while idle logs a splice and opens no turn
Golden event sequence of a three-step turn with tool calls
Replay helper: replayed log gives the same history and every request rebuilds equal
A failed step pairs every unanswered call before step/end
Retry inside one step: one record per attempt, users admitted once, attempt cap, cancellable wait
A failing interception listener ends the turn and not the loop; a failing notice listener is contained
PreStep decisions: Reject gives blocked with name and reason; Enter replaces the batch
TurnStopping is monotonic in every listener order
Stream frames: one Start, dense indexes, one End after the durable record
Each cancel cause reaches turn/end; the first cause wins
Cancel mid-stream commits the interrupted prefix without tool calls
Cancel mid-batch: started calls settle, the rest get paired aborted results in model order
Step-scope cancel keeps the turn when steering is pending; the inbox choice is required
Creation rollback on setup error, listener error and owner disposal; a self-wait returns an error
Teardown points occur in the order T1 to T8 and concurrent disposers share one run
Root disposal during a turn flushes the final turn/end; a flush failure is returned
The step limit ends the turn as budget after the step closed; time limit and override
Model selection precedence, one capture per step, no-model error, switch notice
A preset default registered in a scope wins for its agents; Save goes through config.Service.Apply; a shadowed or failed write is reported
Configured agents: three start modes, duplicate identity refused, one failed start does not stop the others
The step tool set is stable across a retry; key conflicts form a barrier; unknown is exclusive
Composition: a stub factory replaces the driver; nothing imports the driver package
Budget: continuing a long session reaches the first model request inside its budget, also in the memory-limited rerun
A real multi-step turn is bracketed and reconstructable
Cancelling a real stream keeps what was shown and records the cause
Stopping and killing the host leave an honest log
The budget stops a real tool loop
